hints.title: Rewrite before differentiating
hints.body: Divide the numerator terms by the cube-root denominator separately. Write the result as a difference of powers of x.
hints.recap: Roots and quotients can be rewritten as powers before differentiation.
hints.pitfall: Use the real cube root for negative x, and keep x=0 excluded.
hints.pause: Differentiate each power and factor the result.

recall.reminder: Roots and quotients can be rewritten as powers before differentiation.

hints.title: Make a sign table
hints.body: Mark every derivative zero and the excluded input on a number line. Work out the signs of the numerator and denominator on each interval.
hints.recap: A negative derivative means the graph falls as x increases.
hints.pitfall: Keep the leading minus sign; an odd power of a real cube root has the same sign as x.
hints.pause: Find all decreasing intervals. Check whether a stationary endpoint can be included.

recall.reminder: A negative derivative means the graph falls as x increases.

solution:
1. Rewrite and differentiate. f(x)=x−2/3−x1/3 for x≠0, so f′(x)=−23x−5/3−13x−2/3=−x+23x5/3.

2. Check the signs around both boundaries. When x<−2, both x+2 and x5/3 are negative, so the leading minus makes the derivative negative. When −2<x<0, the numerator is positive and denominator negative, so the derivative is positive. When x>0, both are positive, so the derivative is negative.

3. State the decreasing intervals. The function decreases up to its stationary point at x=−2, and also on the positive part of its domain. Thus the intervals are x≤−2 or x>0. Including the stationary endpoint does not stop the function from being decreasing on the left interval; zero is outside the domain.

Answer A.
